Maintenance audit — 30 October 2026

Source: MAINTENANCE.md

Baseline: 820d8c96b15aa20e3e765fda3b16b2adf724375c. Work is isolated from the original checkout. Existing authors, examples and source data remain the provenance of this project.

Purpose and acceptance criteria

bambamR serves researchers importing RNA-seq counts or reads, producing QC, normalization, differential expression and plots through R or a local Shiny app. The immediate release criterion is preservation of sample identity and explicit failure when an analysis cannot be completed. No silent sample removal, alignment replacement, malformed input acceptance or stale analysis display is acceptable. Minimal CRAN-only use must have a runnable example; optional engines must be distinguished from tested configurations.

Prioritized roadmap

  1. Essential: sample and calculation integrity. Separate FASTQ outputs, preserve sample names into counts, require exact metadata matching, validate counts and TPM lengths, respect statistical designs and contrasts. Validate with independent numerical examples and multi-sample regression fixtures.
  2. Essential: external command failures. Quote arguments, separate SAM from diagnostics, check exit status and products, protect existing outputs, and request paired-fragment counts explicitly. Exercise real subprocesses with paths containing spaces and injected failures, plus supported native tools where available.
  3. Everyday use: honest pipeline/app state. Stop on failed requested DE, report plotting failures, clear old app results when inputs change, validate uploads and FASTQ records. Exercise a complete counts workflow and Shiny server state transitions, including failures.
  4. Release evidence. Synchronize function help, examples and migration notes; build/install/check a source package, test the installed first-use path and report optional backends and hosted CI separately. Full real-data validation and cross-platform external-tool qualification remain release gates where this machine cannot supply evidence.

Longer-term work: an explicit paired-end sample sheet, streaming whole-library QC, strand-aware counting options, and workflow resumption. These need a separate design and biological benchmark; they are not inferred from filenames.

Confirmed baseline findings

Severity Evidence/location Impact/action
Critical R/pipeline.R passes one alignment directory to every FASTQ; R/alignment.R uses fixed BAM names Earlier samples overwritten; separate outputs and pass their exact paths onward
High R/alignment.R, R/counting.R, BAM fallbacks ignore process status and pass raw shell arguments False success, mixed SAM/diagnostics, unsafe path handling; checked subprocesses
High R/normalize.R ignores names on TPM lengths and divides zero libraries Incorrect abundance values; align by gene ID and reject invalid divisors
High R/de_analysis.R, .run_de() intersect samples; edgeR ignores the pipeline design; limma indexes original design after contrasts Dropped samples, wrong model or invalid coefficient; strict inputs and explicit model handling
High inst/app/app.R retains old results on uploads and swallows missing DE engines Stale results can be displayed/exported with new counts; invalidate derived state
Medium FASTQ fallback truncates incomplete records; sampling reads the entire file Silent malformed input and unnecessary memory use; bounded reads and validation
Medium Internal counting ignores feature/attribute settings and forces GTF Reject unsupported settings and let annotation format be detected

Baseline and verification

The first test attempt stopped before tests because data.table was missing. After installing CRAN dependencies in a separate audit library, the existing suite passed with 20 skips (mostly optional Bioconductor engines). Baseline green CI and these mocks do not verify native aligners or scientific correctness.

Completed milestones 1–4 locally. Recorded results:

Check Observed result
Regression baseline 23 failing assertions/errors in the new integrity suite before repairs
Full test suite 164 tests, 313 passing assertions, zero failures/errors/warnings; 8 skips for dependency-missing branches in the fully provisioned environment
R CMD check --as-cran 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 NOTE (new submission), including examples, donttest examples, vignette rebuilds, HTML help and indexed PDF manual
Native integration minimap2 2.31 + samtools 1.25 + featureCounts 2.0.2; two samples retain expected counts; internal/external counts agree on the fixture; a paired fragment counts once

Shiny Server tests exercise normalization, settings changes, valid/invalid uploads, missing-engine failures and mismatched metadata; no browser end-to-end test is claimed

Static checks Actionlint and diff whitespace checks pass; standard package lint has zero findings when evaluated with the package namespace loaded; house-style findings remain report-only

Environment: Apple Silicon macOS 27.0.1, R 4.6.1, data.table 1.18.6.1, ggplot2 4.0.3, DESeq2 1.52.0, edgeR 4.10.7, limma 3.68.5, ShortRead 1.70.0, Rsamtools 2.28.0, GenomicAlignments 1.48.0, GenomicFeatures 1.64.0, txdbmaker 1.8.0 and shiny 1.14.0.

Validation commands (after installing the required check tools/dependencies):

Rscript --vanilla -e 'testthat::test_local()'
R CMD build .
R CMD check --as-cran bambamR_0.1.0.tar.gz
R CMD INSTALL bambamR_0.1.0.tar.gz
Rscript --vanilla tools/verify-native.R /new/empty/native-test-directory

The README gives the minimal prerequisites and exact first-use commands. Native integration requires the named tools on PATH plus the internal counting packages. Set BAMBAMR_REQUIRE_ALL_ALIGNERS=true to require STAR and HISAT2 as well; the new Linux CI job does so. Without that setting, absent optional aligners are explicitly reported as not qualified.

The original manual-check failure was missing local TeX/makeindex, resolved by isolated audit tools. pkgdown 2.2.1 emits upstream Pandoc math-option deprecation warnings; the rendered site and local links pass. Synthetic GTF import warns that no genome assembly version is supplied; the fixture is deliberately synthetic.

Remaining gates and next actions

For each published revision, observe hosted CI, including native STAR and HISAT2 and the supported R/OS matrix. Verify the intended Zenodo record/DOI and publication date, then prepare the release/tag and submission with those verified values. The original audit prepared local changes; subsequent source publication does not constitute a release, deployment or submission. Study-specific biological validity and large-data performance are not established by the synthetic fixture. Paired-end sample-sheet automation, streaming QC, strand-aware counting and the house-style/API migration remain deferred.

The audit logs, package archive, hashes, native fixture products and verification receipt are retained outside the checkout in the CTTIR public-maintenance evidence folder. The original working tree was preserved.

Authoritative references checked for this audit:

  • R system2 argument quoting and exit status
  • Subread paired-fragment counting
  • limma reference manual

Additional review findings and release provenance

  • The source archive included a linked-worktree .git pointer and repository-only citation/publication metadata. Explicit build exclusions now keep those files out of the package while retaining them in Git.
  • DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21889924 and the corresponding public Zenodo record both returned HTTP 404 on 30 October 2026; the GitHub release list was empty. .zenodo.json already labels itself a prepared, unpublished draft. The README no longer advertises a published DOI. The old DOI and date remain as comments in CITATION.cff, pending publisher verification, with all authors retained.
  • Oncoplot percentages formerly used only samples with selected mutations. The denominator now includes every sample represented in the input mutation table. Annotation panels share the same grid and sample limits; final PNGs were visually inspected. Heatmaps now render requested annotation tracks and label unscaled values as expression.
  • Attaching the package no longer eagerly loads every optional Bioconductor namespace. Engine functions still check their own runtime requirements.
  • The shared house linter reports existing API names such as padj and pvalue and console output in examples. Renaming the public result schema would be a migration, not a safe maintenance edit. The existing report-only lint setting is unchanged; these findings remain explicitly deferred.

HISAT2 path follow-up — 3 November 2026

The hosted native fixture exposed a second shell parse inside the upstream HISAT2 2.2.1 Perl wrapper. Quoting arguments at R’s outer process boundary does not preserve an index prefix containing spaces across that second parse. The spaces-path acceptance fixture is retained. Inputs needing protection now receive private temporary symbolic links with shell-safe names; complete small/large indexes and compressed FASTQ extensions are preserved. Aliases are removed on success and failure without changing source bytes. Results retain the caller’s original input_paths. Optional arguments containing whitespace or shell metacharacters are rejected explicitly because their arbitrary path/value semantics cannot safely be inferred.

A disposable Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 container reproduced the baseline failure with HISAT2 2.2.1. The repaired external-engine fixture passed real STAR, HISAT2 and minimap2 alignment, exact two-sample gene counts, pipeline execution and paired fragment counting. Additional real HISAT2 checks passed large .ht2l indexes, spaces/apostrophes/semicolon/dollar/comma in paths, gzip and bzip2 reads, paired gzip input and HISAT2_INDEXES lookup, with original checksums unchanged. The native container’s older R/Bioconductor lacks txdbmaker, so its separate external-engine probe explicitly omits the internal-engine assertions; the unchanged complete native CI script remains the hosted acceptance gate. An R startup attempt with a space in TMPDIR was refused by R before package code ran and is not a qualified environment.

Permanent regressions exercise an actual second shell parse, alias cleanup and unsafe optional-argument rejection. The macOS full package suite passed with expected optional-dependency/tool skips. Independent source review found no blocking issue. Existing report-only house lint/API-migration policy is unchanged. Logs, primary wrapper source, synthetic products and exact source identities are under hosted-followup/bambamR/runtime in the external maintenance evidence. Hosted checks for the follow-up commit must still be observed separately.

The first hosted follow-up exposed a Windows-specific path regression: native backslash separators entered the Unix shell-punctuation staging path. The helper now converts those separators only on Windows, before testing whether staging is necessary; the returned original input_paths remain unchanged. Regressions cover drive-prefixed Windows paths and preservation of literal backslashes in Unix filenames, while retaining the original paired-command and native punctuation fixtures. The experimental Ubuntu oldrel-3 dependency job separately cannot resolve optional txdbmaker from Bioconductor3.18; that availability limit is retained, not treated as a successful full-Bioconductor qualification.

A second native Windows run exposed R’s RUNNER~1 short-name spelling after separator normalization. Existing Windows FASTQ paths are now canonicalized before shell admission, using R’s documented expansion of short path elements; bare index names retain HISAT2_INDEXES lookup semantics. The paired-command fixture now supplies a complete eight-part placeholder index, so it remains a valid input when an ambient temporary directory correctly requires staging. Mocked expansion and native Windows shortPathName() regressions retain path identity and source hashes. Native Linux integration passed both preceding repair heads; the latest Windows and complete hosted results remain separately observed gates.
